courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Navigating and Advocating for your Wellness
courses.description: In a time when healthcare is more complex than ever, we often focus on training healthcare providers to communicate effectively for patient safety. However, a crucial piece of the puzzle is missing: who is teaching the patients how to communicate effectively to ensure they receive the highest quality and safest care? Navigating and Advocating for Your Wellness is designed to fill this gap by empowering students with the skills and knowledge they need to successfully navigate the healthcare system and advocate for themselves and their loved ones. The course utilizes TeamSTEPPS strategies, widely recognized in healthcare for enhancing teamwork.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Building Effective Relationships in Healthcare: Carolina Core I
courses.description: This course provides socialization into relationship-centered nursing practice. All Carolina Core tenets are introduced; however, diversity and inclusion, relationship-centered care, and scholarly communication are a central emphasis. Students will obtain a beginning ability to act as a therapeutic agent. Majors Only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Research, Ethics, and Innovation: Carolina Core II
courses.description: This course focuses on research, ethics, and health innovations as a basis for scientific inquiry to address problems that require solutions. All Carolina Core tenets are examined; however, nursing inquiry, evidence-based nursing practice, and ethical conduct in research are central foci. Majors Only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment I: On Campus Clinical I
courses.description: The first in a series of four on campus clinical courses, this course introduces foundational clinical nursing skills and integrates knowledge and skills of comprehensive health assessment for the adult and older adult. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills. Majors Only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment II: On Campus Clinical II
courses.description: This is the second in a series of four on-campus clinical courses with application of advanced clinical nursing skills and comprehensive health assessment to specialized populations. This course emphasizes application of mental health and reproductive health concepts. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills. Majors only.

source.text: NURS 311. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 310 and 330 ; Corequisite, NURS 352 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: The Intersections of Nursing and the Military I
courses.description: This is the first in a series of 3 courses that introduces the discipline, profession, and practice of nursing with a lens on the experiences of nurses and nursing students who have served in the military. History, values, culture, and critical thinking are critical in the discipline of nursing and is explored within this course. Admission to the UNC School of Nursing Military Pathway Program

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: The Intersections of Nursing and the Military II
courses.description: This is the second in a series of 3 courses that discusses the discipline, profession, and practice of nursing with a lens on the experiences of nurses and nursing students who have served in the military. History, values, culture, and critical thinking are critical in the discipline of nursing and is explored within this course.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: The Intersections of Nursing and the Military III
courses.description: This is the last in a series of 3 courses that integrates the discipline, profession, and practice of nursing with a lens on the experiences of nurses and nursing students who have served in the military. History, values, culture, and critical thinking are critical in the discipline of nursing and is explored within this course.

source.text: NURS 318. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 316 and NURS 317 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Culture and Nursing Care
courses.description: Relationship of culture to health and health care practices. Role of culture in structure and delivery of health care in selected countries, and with selected indigenous and minority populations. Majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Applied Global Health Nursing
courses.description: This faculty-led immersion provides students with the opportunity to observe and participate in culturally responsive nursing practice within a global setting or a "local as global" context. Learning experiences may occur internationally or within under-resourced communities of need in the United States. Students will apply nursing knowledge and skills to address the health needs of individuals, families and communities while developing a deeper understanding of global health perspectives.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 4 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: NURS 321. | 2 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, NURS 320 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Nursing Care of Adults I
courses.description: This course considers how nursing influences the health and healing capacities of adults. Students will attain the knowledge necessary to complete a comprehensive assessment of the older adult's physical, functional, psychosocial, and cognitive capacities. Clinical experiences in post-acute care settings provide opportunities for clinical reasoning, clinical care, and knowledge integration. Majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Pathophysiology/Pharmacology Across the Lifespan I
courses.description: Part one of a two-part course series focusing on the physiologic changes that occur as a result of select disease processes. Additionally, the clinical manifestations of altered health and related pharmacotherapy are addressed. Majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Pathophysiology/Pharmacology Across the Lifespan II
courses.description: Part two of a two-part course series focusing on the physiologic changes, the clinical manifestations of altered health, and the pharmacotherapy used to treat complex disease processes. Safe and effective medication administration by the Registered Nurse will be explored. Majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Evidence-Based Care of Older Adults
courses.description: This course emphasizes evidence-based care of the older adult across the care continuum and examines resources available for caregivers of this population.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Family Focused Genomic Health Care
courses.description: This course focuses on the essential competencies in genetics and genomics for all registered nurses. A family perspective is used to help students relate advances in genomics to nursing care. Majors Only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Integrating Principles of Leadership, Quality and Safety, and Informatics into Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course focuses on systems thinking and complexity, development of leadership roles and skills, and interprofessional communication and teamwork. All Carolina Core tenets are examined; however, leadership, quality and safety, and informatics are central foci. Majors Only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Foundations of Population Health and Global Health: Carolina Core IV
courses.description: In this course, all Carolina Core tenets are explored; however, there is a focus on population health and global health as essential components of nursing. Students will examine global health challenges as well as policy strategies of promoting health for all. Majors Only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment III: On Campus Clinical III
courses.description: The third in a series of four on campus clinical courses with application of advanced clinical nursing skills and comprehensive health assessment to specialized populations. This course emphasizes application of leadership, pediatric and community health concepts. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills. Majors Only.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NURS 310, 311, and 352; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 484.

source.text: NURS 410. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 310 , 311 , and 352 ; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 484 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Clinical Nursing Skills and Health Assessment IV: On Campus Clinical IV
courses.description: Fourth in a series of four on-campus clinical courses with application of advanced clinical nursing skills to specialized populations with a focus on transition to practice. The clinical environment is simulated to provide the application of nursing principles and skills.

source.text: NURS 411. | 1 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 310 , 311 , 352 , and 410 ; Corequisite, NURS 697 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Global and Interprofessional Approaches to Solve Complex Cases
courses.description: This course uses a case-based approach to assist students to identify and critically examine challenging issues in health care, develop presentation skills as well as critical thinking from an interprofessional perspective. Students will work in interprofessional teams on a global complex case. Using this approach, students will attain the knowledge necessary to analyze and present results for a comprehensive case at the individual, organizational, and community levels. Open to undergraduate students with permission from instructor.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Nursing Care of Adults II
courses.description: Centers on management of adults experiencing complex health problems and focuses on application of evidence based practice and skill acquisition needed to care for acutely ill patients through transitions in an illness experience. Clinical experience in acute care settings provide application for clinical reasoning, clinical care, and knowledge integration. Majors Only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Exploring Social Determinants of Health Across Populations
courses.description: This seminar allows students to explore how social determinants of health affect the health of populations.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Mental Health Promotion and Psychiatric Care Across Populations and Settings
courses.description: Using selected theories of human psychosocial development, psychopathology, and psychotherapy, this course requires students to advance their use of therapeutic communication skills, examine the range and complexities of human emotional suffering, and apply methods of effective intervention. Majors Only.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NURS 330 and 351; Pre- or corequisites, NURS 311 and 352.

source.text: NURS 481. | 5 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 330 and 351 ; Pre- or corequisites, NURS 311 and 352 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Reproductive Health and Nursing Care of the Childbearing Family
courses.description: The course emphasizes development of caring and critical thinking skills in providing evidence-based nursing care focused on reproductive health and care of childbearing families. Majors Only.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NURS 351 and 330; Pre- or corequisites, NURS 311 and 352.

source.text: NURS 482. | 5 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 351 and 330 ; Pre- or corequisites, NURS 311 and 352 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Family-Centered Nursing Care from Birth through Adolescence
courses.description: This course emphasizes development of caring and critical thinking skills in providing evidence-based, family centered, culturally responsive nursing care to infants, children, and adolescents throughout the care continuum. Majors Only.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NURS 311, 330, and 352; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 430.

source.text: NURS 483. | 5 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 311 , 330 , and 352 ; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 430 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Public Health Nursing in Community Settings
courses.description: Students apply evidence-based public health concepts to community practice to improve health and reduce disparities across the life span, emphasizing interventions using partnership strategies at individual, family, organizational, and policy levels. Majors only.

source.text: NURS 484. | 4 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 311 , 330 , and 352 ; corequisite, NURS 410 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Practicum in Nursing
courses.description: Majors only. The focus of this course is the development of knowledge and experience related to research or service learning and its application to the practice of nursing and health care.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Preparation for Professional Practice
courses.description: This course will assist students in preparation for the NCLEX-RN examination through a strategic and systematic individualized plan of study that utilizes testing programs and other relevant resources.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Management of the Critically Ill Adult
courses.description: This course focuses on collaborative management of critically ill adult patients. Students will gain advanced skills and demonstrate critical thinking to apply evidence based practice to care for critically ill patients across the continuum of care.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Care of Individuals with Cancer and their Families
courses.description: This course focuses on the cancer experience of individuals and families across the lifespan (pediatric to older adults). The cancer control continuum framework will guide content focused discussions on prevention and risk reduction, screening, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and end-of-life care.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NURS 301 and 330; pre- or corequisite, NURS 352.

source.text: NURS 512. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 301 and 330 ; pre- or corequisite, NURS 352 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Pediatric Emergency and Critical Care Fundamentals
courses.description: This course, offered in collaboration with UNC Hospitals, focuses on the collaborative care of pediatric patients in the emergency department and in critical care units (NICU, PICU). Students will be introduced to advanced assessments and interventions utilized in these environments. Students will also discuss interdisciplinary challenges specific to pediatric emergency and critical care and investigate evidence-based solutions to some of these challenges. Majors only.

source.text: NURS 514. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, NURS 483 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: SHAC: Student Health Action Coalition
courses.description: This course provides service-learning opportunities to apply nursing practice within the context of interprofessional care for vulnerable populations by participating with Student Health Action Coalition (SHAC) activities.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 0 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Experiential Learning in Nursing
courses.description: This course provides experiential educational opportunities to apply nursing practice through volunteer participation in select communities. Majors only.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 0 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Interprofessional Team Work and Communication - Key to Patient Safety
courses.description: Majors only. This interprofessional course focuses on understanding roles, teamwork, and communication to improve patient safety within the health care environment. National standards and initiatives will be the foundation of the course. Pass/Fail only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Health Care in the Global Context
courses.description: A faculty-led experiential learning opportunity focusing on development and knowledge related to research, health care systems, or service learning and its application to nursing and health care. Majors only or permission of the instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 8 total credits. 8 total completions.

source.text: NURS 609. | 1 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, NURS 320 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Introductory Spanish for Health Professionals
courses.description: This course is intended for students who know no Spanish or so little that they feel the need to start over. Students with more than two semesters of college Spanish are not eligible. The course covers the curriculum of first-semester Spanish taught within a health context, with a focus on speaking.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Supporting the Childbearing Family
courses.description: Application required. An interprofessional, service-learning approach to studying maternity care. Students will receive professional doula training and volunteer as birth doulas within the Volunteer Doula Service Program at North Carolina Women's Hospital.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Interprofessional Perspectives on Diabetes Mellitus Management
courses.description: This elective course examines the current issues involved in managing diabetes mellitus in persons over their lifespan with an interprofessional lens. Contributions from all members of the healthcare team are an important theme throughout this course. This course integrates the pathophysiology of disease, therapeutics, and psychosocial modalities into the management of patients with diabetes. Previously offered as NURS 516. Majors only.

source.text: NURS 612. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 330 and NURS 351 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Intermediate Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: This intermediate course is the equivalent of the third semester of college Spanish. Students will hone their listening and speaking skills in class primarily through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a health clinic in rural North Carolina.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Spanish for Health Care I
courses.description: Required preparation, third semester Spanish or equivalent. This advanced course reviews the grammar of the third and fourth semester of college Spanish. Students hone their listening and speaking skills through role-playing activities and class discussion. Activities center on an original film set in a Latino-run health clinic.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Experiential Learning in Nursing: A Collaboration with UNC Health Center for Nursing Excellence
courses.description: This course provides experiential educational opportunities to apply nursing practice through volunteer participation in select communities associated with UNC Health. Admission to the undergraduate nursing program required.

source.text: NURS 616. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, NURS 430 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Experiencing Health Professions: A Service-Learning Partnership for Pre-Health Students
courses.description: This course provides experiential service opportunities for career exploration with select communities and populations associated with UNC Health. Students will be assigned to a role within the health system and will complete service hours within their assigned role. Class sessions will include topics related to healthcare and will develop skills in reflection, communication, and teamwork for career development. Does not count as an elective in the BIOL major or minor. It is recommended that students complete BIOL 117 before enrolling in BIOL 119 . Permission of instructor.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Mindfulness and Self-Compassion for Caring Professionals
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce students to rationale, research, and practices of mindfulness and self-compassion. Upon course completion, students will exhibit knowledge and skills related to mindfulness/contemplative practice/training, research evidence on mindfulness for enhancing provider self-care, patient/client engagement, and wellness (e.g., reducing stress, burnout, and fatigue; increasing resilience). Majors only; permission of the instructor for non-majors.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Nursing Inquiry and Evidence-Based Practice for Advanced Scholarship
courses.description: Introduction to scientific inquiry, evidence-based practice, and nursing/healthcare innovations. Emphasis on: theory; ethics; problem identification; question development; design selection; data analysis and interpretation; statistical applications; and appraisal of research reports. Admission to an undergraduate BSN program and eligible to take required undergraduate nursing research course; the Hillman Scholars program; or PhD in Nursing Program required.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Hillman Scholars in Nursing Innovation: Integrative Seminar
courses.description: Cultivates students' development as nurse scientists, scholars, and leaders to improve health care quality, safety, and delivery, and to influence policies that promote health and strengthen health systems outcomes. Admission to the Hillman Scholars Program in Nursing Innovation is required.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Experimental Courses
courses.description: Pilot test for new courses in the nursing program.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Care of the Dying and Bereaved throughout the Life Span
courses.description: Students from a variety of health sciences-related disciplines gain an understanding of issues in working with dying and bereaved individuals of all ages and their families.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Honors in Nursing, Part I
courses.description: Permission of the program director. Majors only. Preparation of a two-semester honors project under the direction of department advisors.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Honors in Nursing, Part II
courses.description: Permission of the program director. Majors only. Preparation of a two-semester honors project under the direction of department advisors.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Capstone: Transitions in Care and Practice
courses.description: Students will incorporate previously learned leadership concepts, clinical skills, therapeutic communication, and critical thinking to deliver quality nursing care, using evidence based practice, in varied settings with faculty and RN guidance. Preparing for the NCLEX-RN examination and strategies for successful transition from student nurse to registered nurse will be explored. Majors only.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NURS 330, 430, 481, 482, and 483; Corequisites, NURS 402 and 411.

source.text: NURS 697. | 6 Credits. | Prerequisites, NURS 330 , 430 , 481 , 482 , and 483 ; Corequisites, NURS 402 and 411 . | HI-INTERN.

courses.title: Alternative Medicine

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Scientific Writing
courses.description: Focuses on the principles and practice of scientific writing, with emphasis on research proposals, theses, research reports, dissertations, and articles for publication.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Developmental Physiology and Pathophysiology
courses.description: This course explores developmental changes in morphological processes and normal and pathologic physiology in humans from conception through adolescence. Physiological differences between infants and children and adults are emphasized.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Pathophysiology for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course explores the physiologic functions in humans throughout the lifespan. The broad-based content integrates pathophysiological concepts with emphasis on advanced practice nursing. Must be enrolled in School of Nursing Graduate Program.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Pharmacotherapeutics for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course will examine the principles of pharmacotherapeutic decision-making in advanced nursing practice, with application to the clinical management of common health problems specific to all age groups, encompassing a life span approach. Nursing majors only.

source.text: NURS 720. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or Co-requisite, NURS 715 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Pediatric Pharmacology
courses.description: The course will examine the principles of pharmacotherapeutic decision making in advanced nursing practice, with application to the clinical management of common health problems specific to pediatrics.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Psychopharmacology in Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing
courses.description: Examines the principles of psychopharmacology and neurobiology for safe and effective psychotherapeutic management of individuals with psychiatric and mental health problems across the lifespan.

courses.title: Psychopharmacology for Advanced Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing
courses.description: This course introduces evidence-based psychopharmacological principles for the management of psychiatric-mental health conditions.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment and Diagnostic Reasoning in Pediatric Nursing
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare the advanced practice nurse to comprehensively assess pediatric clients using a diagnostic reasoning process.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 8 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Health Assessment and Diagnostic Reasoning in Primary Care Nursing
courses.description: This course examines the process of diagnostic reasoning as a framework to synthesize comprehensive assessment of patients throughout the lifespan.

source.text: NURS 726. | 4 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, NURS 715 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Diagnostic Process in Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing
courses.description: The course introduces you to the psychiatric-mental health specialty of nurse practitioners. It evaluates and enhances competencies in gathering information to conduct a comprehensive psychiatric assessment and synthesize diagnoses. Through the course, students learn the clinical and theoretical reasoning processes for developing and validating psychiatric diagnoses and using models for assessing individuals.

source.text: NURS 727. | 2 Credits. | Pre- or corequisites, NURS 715 and 750 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Foundations in Clinical Informatics: Data, Information, and Knowledge
courses.description: Required preparation, graduate nursing program admission or instructor permission. This foundational course provides an overview of computer and information science concepts as applied to health care.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Evidence-Based Practice and Research
courses.description: This course provides the essential concepts and strategies for research and quality improvement, and the impact of these methodologies on patient populations and care systems.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Health Care Policy and Leadership
courses.description: This course examines the role of nursing in health care leadership and policy. Students will gain competencies in the application of micro and meso level leadership tools. Students will apply these skills to the health policy development and advocacy as a means of impacting the health of populations at the local, state, and national and/or international level. Nursing majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Health and Physical Assessment for Advanced Nursing Practice
courses.description: This course is an advanced, comprehensive assessment of an individual's health across their developmental lifespan that examines the interactions of developmental, biopsychosocial, and socio-cultural contexts of health.

source.text: NURS 750. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, NURS 715 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Diagnostic Reasoning
courses.description: This course examines the process of diagnostic reasoning as a framework to synthesize comprehensive assessment and disease prevention using lifespan concepts. Nursing majors only.
courses.requisites_raw: Corequisite, NURS 750; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 715.

source.text: NURS 752. | 2 Credits. | Corequisite, NURS 750 ; Pre- or corequisite, NURS 715 .

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Research for Advanced Clinical Practice
courses.description: Graduate standing and successful completion of an undergraduate statistics course required. This course explores approaches to research problems in advanced practice nursing. Theories, methods, designs, measurement, ethical conduct, and skills in critical appraisal are emphasized.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Intermediate Statistical Applications in Health Care
courses.description: Graduate standing required. This course provides an introduction to probability, statistical concepts, and analytical techniques useful in health care research and for interpreting the literature.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Interpreting Research Reports
courses.description: For Nursing students admitted to the Graduate School. Focuses on approaches for critical reading of research reports to evaluate the evidence base for practice.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Synthesis and Translation of Evidence
courses.description: Focuses on the translation of research evidence to support improved models of care delivery.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Multidisciplinary Perspectives on Managing Diabetes Mellitus
courses.description: This course examines the current issues involved in managing diabetes mellitus in persons over their life span. Contributions of the multidisciplinary team are an important theme throughout this course.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Genomics and Society
courses.description: This multidisciplinary course offers students the opportunity to gain a basic understanding of human genetics and explore the ethical, legal, and social implications of recent advances in genetics.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Concepts in the Clinical Care of Older Adults
courses.description: Graduate students only. Focuses on advanced concepts for nursing management of older adults and their families with an emphasis on interdisciplinary care.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Cancer Care for Advanced Practice Providers
courses.description: This course for MSN, DNP, and PhD students provides an understanding of management of adults across the cancer continuum (prevention, early detection, treatment, and beyond [survivorship, palliative care, end-of-life care]) for advanced practice providers regardless of practice setting.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Pharmacology in Oncology
courses.description: Focuses on the pharmacologic management of drugs used for therapeutic management and supportive care in adult oncology.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, NURS 715 and 720; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Concepts in Oncology Nursing
courses.description: Admission to Adult-Gerontology Nurse Practitioner program or permission of the instructor required. This course focuses on an evidence-based approach for the advanced practice nurse, incorporating pathophysiology; prevention/detection; medical treatment; nursing management; and socioeconomic, ethical, and legal issues related to adult cancer care.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Population Health: Interprofessional Management in a Changing Healthcare System
courses.description: This interprofessional education course focuses on preparing healthcare professionals with the foundational skills needed to work in teams to effectively collaborate and coordinate care in population health. Admission to the School of Nursing graduate program or graduate students in any of the Health Affairs Schools with permission of instructor required.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Primary Care of Adolescents and Adults
courses.description: This course will focus on advanced assessment, diagnosis and management of adolescents and adults seen in primary care settings.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Crafting Effective Health Research Grant Proposals
courses.description: In this course students will apply their foundational knowledge of scientific theory, methods and analysis to design a research proposal. They will generate ideas and drafts of the Specific Aims, Significance, Innovation, and Methods sections of the proposal. While students are encouraged to search and apply for NIH and non-NIH grants, the course will focus on the NIH research proposal since it is the major funding source for health-related biomedical research. The final product will include a full draft of the research plan for an NIH F31 grant proposal or equivalent (e.g., foundation grant, K99).

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Qualitative Approaches to Scientific Inquiry
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive examination of qualitative research methodologies, including qualitative description, grounded theory, ethnography, and narrative inquiry. Students will critically examine the philosophical underpinnings of these approaches and their application to scientific inquiry. Emphasis is placed on designing qualitative studies, with a focus on sampling strategies, data collection techniques, data analysis processes, and the representation of findings. The course also addresses essential considerations for ensuring validity and rigor, ethical research practices, and strategies for managing challenges in qualitative research.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Quantitative Approaches to Scientific Inquiry
courses.description: This course offers an in-depth introduction to quantitative research methods. It focuses on designing studies, including descriptive, associational, explanatory, and predictive designs, as well as sampling, measurement, data collection, analysis, and result interpretation. Students will explore the philosophical foundations of these methods and their application in scientific inquiry. The course also covers key aspects of validity, rigor, ethical practices, and strategies for overcoming challenges in quantitative research.

courses.subject: NURS

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Theoretical Principles of Evidence-Based Practice
courses.description: This course is an analysis of the theoretical principles of translating, disseminating, and implementing evidence into healthcare practice. Students will evaluate major theoretical and conceptual models in the fields of translational science, dissemination and implementation, organizational change, and quality improvement. Nursing majors only.

courses.subject: NURS

courses.title: Experiential Learning I: Statistical Analysis
courses.description: This course will introduce and prepare students for biostatistical computing of quantitative data using mainly SAS statistical software. It builds on the knowledge obtained in NURS 916 : Design Measurement and Analysis: Descriptive & Associational Research by reinforcing the material and focusing on application within the SAS framework. Course prepares students for future SAS programming and analysis needs in NURS 917 : Design Measurement and Analysis: Explanatory and Predictive Research and NURS 918 : Intermediate Statistics: Regression Analysis.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Foundations of Statistical Analysis
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to statistical analysis for quantitative data, combining theoretical concepts with practical applications through various software programs (e.g., SAS, G*Power, and nQuery). Students will learn core methods such as descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square tests, and correlation, along with an introduction to advanced topics like regression, moderation, mediation, sample size calculation, and handling missing data. Emphasis is placed on interpreting statistical results, data visualization, and communicating APA-style results.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Clinical Scholarship and Professional Communication
courses.description: This course provides students with a foundation in professional communication of scholarly and clinical work through a variety of strategies. Nursing majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Leading Organizational and Systems Change
courses.description: This course provides a foundation for the application of core leadership principles to lead organizational change within complex and dynamic healthcare systems. Students will gain competencies in the application of macro-level leadership tools (e.g., organizational assessment, systems thinking, strategic planning, workforce management, and organizational policy development and analysis) to address service delivery challenges and drive organizational change, with a particular focus on quality improvement and patient safety initiatives. Nursing majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Informatics for Safe and Effective Health Care
courses.description: This course prepares health care leaders to effectively select, implement and utilize health information systems for effective delivery of health care services and promote quality, safety and patient engagement.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Public Policy and Advocacy in Health Care
courses.description: This course examines the intersection of health policy development, advocacy and nursing as a means of impacting the health of populations at the local, state, national and/or international level. Emerging issues in health policy will be explored with an emphasis placed on transformational leadership principles as a means of influencing change. Nursing majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Leadership I: Operational Effectiveness
courses.description: This course allows the learner to examine personal values, strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats as they relate to successful leadership practices and behaviors in complex health care organizations. Nursing majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Advanced Leadership II: Strategic Effectiveness
courses.description: This course builds upon foundational leadership knowledge to incorporate executive practices essential to successfully leading larger health care delivery systems and health professions organizations into the future. Nursing majors only.

courses.subject: NURS
courses.title: Measurement and Data Quality in Health Research
courses.description: This course will examine the links between measurement theory and practice, emphasizing study design, data collection methods, and data quality. Students will critically evaluate concepts underlying measurement reliability and validity and explore the construction of measurement tools and their use in quantitative research. The course will incorporate a combination of theory, methods, and practical skill development, including training in statistical software (e.g., SAS, SPSS, or Stata) for factor analysis and computation of reliability measures. Students will be prepared to critically evaluate methodological issues in quantitative measurement and develop measurement approaches for research proposals. Permission of the instructor for students lacking the required preparation.
